channel.title: Fadak AI blog
channel.description: Notes from the face: underground development, per-round measurement and the mining labour gap.

item.title: Mine-to-mill: how the blast sets up the mill's day
item.author: ali@fadakai.com (Ali)
item.description: The size of the rock leaving a blast decides how hard the mill has to work. Here is what published drill-to-mill projects have reported, what they cost, and why the gains only last if someone keeps measuring.

item.title: What a metre of development really costs
item.author: ali@fadakai.com (Ali)
item.description: Published Canadian cost data puts a metre of lateral development in the thousands of dollars, and much of that cost is paid per round, not per metre. Here is where a few points of pull show up in the budget and the schedule.

item.title: The 2026 mining labour gap, and what it means at the face
item.author: ali@fadakai.com (Ali)
item.description: Canada's mining industry needs a quarter of a million hires in a decade, and the hardest jobs to fill are often the most physical. A look at the numbers and where technology can actually help.

item.title: Pull, overbreak and fragmentation: the three numbers in every round
item.author: ali@fadakai.com (Ali)
item.description: A plain guide to the three things a development blast either gets right or wrong, what each one costs, and why measuring them every round is harder than it sounds.

item.title: Why we started with the development round
item.author: ali@fadakai.com (Ali)
item.description: Every round underground needs experienced eyes after the blast. Experienced people are getting harder to find. That gap is what Fadak AI is built around.
